name: Darryl Kropp
bio: Darryl Kropp has lived in Abbotsford for more than 25 years and leads human services implementations at RedMane Technology; he previously built a lean management system at Cascade Aerospace. He was elected to the First West Credit Union board in 2018 and served 17 years on the Northview Community Church board, 11 as Chair. He holds the ICD.D designation from the Rotman School of Management and is a certified PMP.

name: Lakhwinder Jhaj
bio: Lakhwinder Jhaj immigrated from India to Mission as a child in 1976 and has lived in the Fraser Valley since 2010. She has more than 20 years of experience operating a construction company and used vehicle dealership and is a former reporter. She has served as Vice-President of Apna Homes Society, and ran for the BC NDP in 2009 and 2013 and for the federal Liberals in 2021.

name: Pam Alexis
occupation: Former MLA; former Mayor of Mission
bio: Pam Alexis was elected Mayor of Mission in 2018 and MLA for Abbotsford-Mission in 2020, and served as Minister of Agriculture and Food. She has served on the boards of the Mission Chamber of Commerce and the Mission Rotary Club.

name: Virender Dass
bio: Virender Dass is the OneBC candidate for Abbotsford-Mission. He came to Canada in 2014 after 18 years working in visual effects and founded the Abbotsford health supplement company Wellness Extract in 2017. He and his wife run a children's mental-math learning centre, and he founded the Santosh Care Foundation, a registered charity.

name: Bruce Banman
bio: Bruce Banman has been MLA for Abbotsford South since 2020 and joined the Conservative Party of BC in September 2023, when he was appointed House Leader. He has lived in Abbotsford since 1982 and previously served as an Abbotsford city councillor and mayor. Before politics he worked as a chiropractor and owned a small business.

name: Leah Ballantyne
bio: Leah Ballantyne (Mikisew Iskwew) is a lawyer and the first member of her Cree Nation to become a lawyer, with nearly two decades of practice advising First Nations, governments and international bodies. She is a graduate of Douglas College and UBC Law and holds a Master of Laws from the University of Hawaii. She has served as vice-chair of a health authority board and on the BCIT board.

name: Robin Roy
bio: Robin Roy is the OneBC candidate for Abbotsford South, where he lives. He previously ran construction companies in Victoria and the Lower Mainland, and since 1998 has operated a computer service company. He is married with three adult children.

name: Gurpreet Chahal
bio: Gurpreet Singh Chahal has lived in the Fraser Valley for 25 years and has worked as a real estate professional for 20 years. He has volunteered with organizations including Sahit Academy, Abbotsford Field Hockey Club, Mission Community Services Society and Mission's Social Development Planning Committee.

name: Jules Côté
bio: Jules Côté was born and raised in Abbotsford and is a political science student at the University of the Fraser Valley. She is a member of the National Farmers Union and has volunteered with the local food bank and the Starfish Pack Program. She was the NDP candidate in Mission-Matsqui-Abbotsford in the 2025 federal election.

name: Korky Neufeld
bio: Korky Neufeld began his career in church ministry as a pastor in Vancouver and later led a church in Abbotsford for over a decade, and has worked as Construction Manager for Servicemaster Restore of the Fraser Valley. He served 15 years as an Abbotsford Board of Education trustee, including as Chair and Vice-Chair, and two terms as a director of the BC School Trustees Association.

name: Donegal Wilson
occupation: MLA; former Executive Director, BC Snowmobile Federation
bio: Donegal Wilson was elected MLA for Boundary-Similkameen in 2024 and has served as Official Opposition Critic for Water, Lands and Resource Stewardship and Wildlife, and as Deputy Chair of the Select Standing Committee on Finance and Government Services. She spent more than a decade as Executive Director of the BC Snowmobile Federation and co-owns a small engine business in Keremeos.

name: Keith Pomeroy
bio: Keith Pomeroy is the OneBC candidate for Boundary-Similkameen. He grew up on a farm in B.C.'s Peace Country and worked for 35 years in the oil and gas industry. Since retiring, he has operated a ranch, a gravel pit and quarry, and a small construction business.

name: Roly Russell
bio: Roly Russell was born and raised in rural Grand Forks. As a local leader he worked on disaster recovery following the 2018 Grand Forks floods and the 2021 atmospheric rivers.

name: Ed Ewald
bio: Ed Ewald was born and raised in Smithers and works in local hardware sales after more than 30 years in dairy farming, including 10 years running his own dairy business. He is President of the Christian Heritage Party of BC and of his church council, and has served on the board of a Christian school.

name: Frankie Abel
bio: Frankie Abel is a Gitxsan woman and advisor who grew up in northern B.C. Her work has included cultural safety, Indigenous governance and public policy.

name: Sharon Hartwell
occupation: MLA; business owner; former Mayor of Telkwa
bio: Sharon Hartwell was born and raised in the Bulkley Valley and is a business owner. She served a term and a half on Telkwa Village Council and 12 years as Mayor of Telkwa, was the Small Community Representative at UBCM, and chaired the North West Regional Hospital District.

name: Anne Kang
bio: Anne Kang has been MLA for Burnaby Centre since 2017 and has lived in Burnaby for more than 40 years. She is a former Burnaby teacher and served three terms as a Burnaby City Councillor.

name: Joshua Domnich
bio: Joshua Domnich holds a Bachelor of Arts in Criminology from Simon Fraser University. He has worked as a Community Liaison Officer for a federal Conservative MP and as a Legislative Assistant for the Conservative Party of BC caucus, and has served as a campaign manager and riding association treasurer. He previously spent more than a decade in landscaping operations and management.

name: Shila Taheri
bio: Shila Taheri is a legal researcher and published author who holds an LL.M. in International Business Law and an LL.B. She holds elected roles in the BC General Employees' Union, including First Vice-Chair of Local 803 and Chair of the Component 8 Membership Committee, and has represented workers in grievances and workplace disputes.

name: Vikas Gautam
bio: Vikas Gautam is a communications and event organizer who has volunteered with the Hindu Temple Burnaby and supported fundraising for the Surrey Food Bank, Vancouver Food Bank and B.C. flood relief. During the COVID-19 pandemic he organized online events connecting people internationally.

name: De Ding
bio: De Ding is the OneBC candidate for Burnaby East. He is an engineer who spent 20 years working on energy projects outside B.C. before returning to care for his mother. He lives in Burnaby with his two children.

name: Javad Shushtarian
bio: Javad Shushtarian has lived in Burnaby's Forest Grove neighbourhood for 23 years. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Nursing from BCIT and a Bachelor of Science in Biology from Simon Fraser University, and has worked as a student nurse with Vancouver Coastal Health. He has volunteered with the BC Cancer Agency, Vancouver General Hospital's emergency department and Guru Nanak's Free Kitchen.

name: Peter Si
bio: Peter Si moved to Burnaby at age 12 and holds a Bachelor of Arts from the University of Alberta. He has worked on municipal, provincial and federal campaigns, has been President of the Richmond-Queensborough riding association since 2024, and has worked for the Conservative caucus in Victoria for the past two years.

name: Rohini Reah Arora
bio: Rohini Arora was first elected MLA for Burnaby East in 2024 and served as Deputy Chair of the BC Government Caucus. She grew up in Burnaby East's Westridge neighbourhood and previously served as Director of Organizing and Campaigns at the BC Federation of Labour.

name: Joe Latam
bio: Joe Latam was born and raised in British Columbia and is a member of Métis Nation BC. He holds a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from UBC, began his career in the agriculture and manufacturing industries, and has worked for the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia for the past two years.

name: Raj Chouhan
occupation: MLA; Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
bio: Raj Chouhan moved to Canada in 1973 and has been elected MLA six times; he is the first South Asian person to serve as Speaker of the BC legislature. He was the founding President of the Canadian Farmworkers' Union and a founding member of the BC Organization to Fight Racism.

name: Janet Routledge
bio: Janet Routledge worked for members of the Public Service Alliance of Canada for three decades, including on pay equity in the federal public service. As MLA she served as Parliamentary Secretary for Labour.

name: Jenny Yamagata
bio: Jenny Yamagata is the OneBC candidate for Burnaby North and has lived in Burnaby for 15 years. She founded the non-profit Women's Oasis for Maternal Wellness & Birth (WOMB) and previously worked in administration and at her family's glass art studio. She has volunteered as a Girl Guide leader for six years.

name: Maddy Kennedy-Parrott
bio: Maddy Kennedy-Parrott is a civil engineer and an Associate at a building-science consulting firm, working on deep energy retrofits and climate-resilient buildings. She holds a civil engineering degree from Queen's University and a Master of Engineering in Building Science from BCIT, has taught at Langara College, Brighton College and BCIT, and has served on the BC Greens Provincial Council.

name: Simon Chandler
bio: Simon Chandler has lived in North Burnaby for fifteen years and holds a Bachelor of Business Administration in accounting from Trinity Western University. He has worked in public practice accounting, served as a Community Police Volunteer for three years, and served as an infantry soldier in the Canadian Army Reserves.

name: Andrew Rose
bio: Andrew Rose is the OneBC candidate for Burnaby South-Metrotown. He studied computer science at Brock University and worked at Amazon.com in Seattle before moving to British Columbia in 2002. He lives in Burnaby South with his family and serves on a school parent advisory council.

name: Bryan Fockler
bio: Bryan Fockler works as a delivery driver in South Burnaby and has a background in project management. He has worked with the environmental non-profit Earthwatch and the International Organization for Migration, and serves on a Joint Health and Safety Committee.

name: David Xie
bio: David Xie has lived in Burnaby for nearly a decade and is a graduate of the University of British Columbia. He has worked in recruitment and talent acquisition for more than a decade.

name: Paul Choi
bio: Paul Choi was first elected MLA for Burnaby South-Metrotown in 2024 and served as Parliamentary Secretary for Trade and as First Vice-President of the Pacific NorthWest Economic Region. He is a former police officer and has worked as a small business owner and lawyer, and is a Qualified Mediator and Arbitrator.

name: Douglas Gook
bio: Douglas Gook has spent his adult life in the Cariboo-Chilcotin and owns Silvequus Selection Systems; he was a founding member of the Cariboo Horse Loggers Association. He served for many years as a director of the BC Environmental Network and the Canadian Environmental Network, and has been a founding director of Spirit Dance Cooperative Community for nearly 25 years.

name: Kathryn Askew
bio: Kathryn Askew is a retired public school teacher with 32 years in education who served as a local teachers' union president and bargaining chair. She lives at Canim Lake and volunteers with the Hawkins Lake Volunteer Fire Department, Forest Grove Legion and Canim Lake Community Club.

name: Lorne Doerkson
bio: Lorne Doerkson has lived in the Cariboo for close to thirty years and spent twenty years as a Black Press newspaper publisher before moving into financial planning. He has been a small-business owner, Rotary president and rodeo announcer. In September he was chosen by caucus colleagues to lead the party into the 45th General Election.

name: A'aliya Warbus
occupation: MLA; Director of Cultural Communications; professor
bio: Á'a:líya Warbus was born and raised in Stó:lō Territory and holds a Master of Fine Arts in Film Production from UBC. She has worked as Director of Cultural Communications at Stó:lō Xwexwilmexw Government and as a professor in the Indigenous Digital Film department at Capilano University, and is a filmmaker, podcast host, actor and musician.

name: Kelli Paddon
bio: Kelli Paddon is a former MLA and served as Parliamentary Secretary for Gender Equity. She is the founder of Equiiti Strategic, a Chilliwack-based consulting and leadership coaching business.

name: Adila Shaukat
bio: Adila Shaukat is a scientist who holds a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology from Imperial College London. She has worked with local non-profits and in the public service.

name: Dan Grice
bio: Dan Grice is a real estate and estate planning lawyer with 12 years of experience and has lived in North Chilliwack since graduating from Robson Hall Law School in 2013. He studied classical history and archaeology at UBC and was an organizer in the 2005 and 2009 electoral reform referendums. He previously ran as an independent candidate.

name: Heather Maahs
bio: Heather Maahs was first elected as a Chilliwack school trustee in 2008 and was re-elected in subsequent elections. She moved to Chilliwack from North Vancouver in 1993, where she and her husband ran a construction company, and has trained in Orton Gillingham tutoring.

name: Andrea Dunlop
bio: Andrea Dunlop was a high school teacher for three decades and grew up in small-town BC. She has been a board member of the Windermere Community Association for ten years.

name: Rana Nelson
bio: Rana Nelson is a high-school teacher in Revelstoke with a Bachelor of Education and has 30 years of experience in writing, editing and research. She has served as a director of the Revelstoke Community Housing Society and on the Columbia Basin Regional Advisory Committee, and was the Green Party candidate in Kootenay-Columbia in the 2021 federal election.

name: Scott McInnis
bio: Scott McInnis has lived in Kimberley since 2010 and has worked for 15 years as a teacher and principal in public and independent schools. He volunteers with Elks Lodge #90 in Kimberley and participated in the Teacher Institute for Parliamentary Democracy in 2022.

name: Jodie Wickens
bio: Jodie Wickens was elected MLA in 2016 and again in 2024, and served as Minister of Children and Family Development. She previously served as Director of Programs and Services for Child and Youth Programs at a large non-profit.

name: Kaden Mann
bio: Kaden Mann was born and raised in Coquitlam. He has a background in psychology and criminology and experience in security and public safety.

name: Ryan Peterson
bio: Ryan Peterson co-founded Finger Food Studios in Port Coquitlam in 2011 and, after its acquisition by Unity Technologies, led a global division there. He was elected Chair of the Business Council of British Columbia in 2026 before stepping away to run, and serves on the board of the Rick Hansen Foundation. He has lived in the Tri-Cities since 2014.

name: Valerie Morrison
bio: Valerie Morrison has worked in animation for more than two decades, including on 12 feature films, television, video games and digital media. She has lived in British Columbia for 14 years and serves as Vice-President of her townhouse community's strata council.

name: Jennifer Blatherwick
bio: Jennifer Blatherwick was elected MLA for Coquitlam-Maillardville in 2024. She previously served two terms as a Coquitlam School Board trustee and as Executive Director of a not-for-profit for at-risk youth.

name: Matt Liang
bio: Matt Liang has served as a Deputy Sheriff, worked as a Child Care Counsellor, and worked as a health and safety facilitator for the BC Public Service and the BC General Employees' Union. He has volunteered with Special Olympics BC, the Share Society food bank, the RCMP and St. Paul's Advocacy Office.

name: Nicola Spurling
bio: Nicola Spurling has operated a renovation and construction business since 2011. She is the founder of Tri-Cities Pride, sits on the board of QMUNITY, and has served as the BC Greens' Lower Mainland representative since 2017. She ran in the 2017, 2020 and 2024 provincial elections and the 2018 Coquitlam municipal election.

name: Brennan Day
bio: Brennan Day is a long-time Comox Valley resident who served as Executive Director of the Eureka Support Society. He previously managed international projects and founded an industrial supply, manpower and training firm.

name: Jason Cook
bio: Jason Cook is a Courtenay resident with more than two decades of experience in foreign exchange and capital markets. He volunteers with Habitat for Humanity on the Family Services Selection Committee.

name: Jay Van Oostdam
bio: Jay Van Oostdam is a veterinarian with a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine from the University of Saskatchewan and a Master of Public Health from the University of Minnesota. He had a 25-year career with Health Canada and BC Environment studying environmental contaminants, including leading the Human Health component of the federal Northern Contaminants Program.

name: Will Cole-Hamilton
bio: Will Cole-Hamilton is a former small business owner with a background in law who has been elected twice to Courtenay City Council and serves as Chair of the Comox Valley Regional District. He led the creation of the Comox Valley Housing Authority.

name: Bert Chen
bio: Bert Chen owns a Vancouver Island firm that provides project management and construction services for power plants and other large industries across Canada. He has worked in remote communities across Canada, including with First Nations on infrastructure projects, and has served as long-time finance director of the BC Elks Association.

name: Debra Toporowski
occupation: MLA; former municipal and First Nation councillor
bio: Debra Toporowski (Qwulti’stunaat) was first elected MLA in 2024. A member of Cowichan Tribes, she previously served two terms as a councillor for the Municipality of North Cowichan and five terms as a councillor of Cowichan Tribes.

name: James Chumsa
bio: James Chumsa was born and raised in the Cowichan Valley and graduated from Vancouver Island University in 2019 with a Bachelor of Arts in sociology. He was the Communist Party candidate in Nanaimo-Ladysmith in the 2019 federal election and is active with several grassroots organizations in the Cowichan Valley.

name: Justin Douglas
bio: Justin Douglas is a small-business owner and lawyer by training who co-founded EMBER Studios Duncan and VIT Management. He holds a political science degree from the University of Victoria and common law and civil law degrees from McGill University, and has worked in immigration and refugee law, legal information services, restorative justice and non-profit organizations.

name: Kuldeep Rangi
bio: Kuldeep Rangi operates a real estate marketing brokerage and previously spent nearly a decade in banking with Scotiabank and First West Credit Union. He lives in Delta North and has been involved in local organizations and community sports.

name: Monica Mohan
bio: Monica Mohan is a practising lawyer and North Delta resident who holds a degree in Administration of Justice from Penn State and a law degree from the United States. She previously worked in civilian roles with the Vancouver Police Department and Guelph Police Service, and as a victim advocate and sexual assault counsellor. She speaks English, Punjabi and Hindi.

name: Todd Schierling
bio: Todd Schierling is President of the BC Professional Firefighters’ Association and a Suppression Fire Captain with Surrey Fire Service, where he has served since 1996. He has served on the BC Municipal Pension Plan, the BC Federation of Labour Executive Council and the BC First Responders Mental Health Committee, and helped launch a high school girls’ basketball tournament in 2001.

name: Ian Paton
bio: Ian Paton is a lifelong Delta South resident who has served as MLA for Delta South since 2017, including as Shadow Minister for Agriculture and Food. He has over 30 years of experience owning and running a dairy farm and farm auction business, and was elected to Delta council in 2010. He is a past president of the East Delta Community Hall Society and a former volunteer firefighter.

name: Jason McCormick
bio: Jason McCormick is a TransLink bus driver and union activist who is involved in the BC cycling community and the South Delta Basketball Association. He and his wife raised their three children in Ladner.

name: Jim McMurtry
bio: Jim McMurtry is the OneBC candidate for Delta South, where he lives. He holds a Ph.D. in Educational Theory from the University of Toronto and has worked as a teacher, principal and college lecturer. He was dismissed by the Abbotsford School District in 2023 following comments about residential schools.

name: Skadi Green
bio: Skadi Green is a Canada Post letter carrier in South Vancouver and a steward and organizer with the Canadian Union of Postal Workers. She previously worked for a decade as a UPS package driver and was a Teamsters member. Originally from New Brunswick, she has lived in the Greater Vancouver region since 2010.

name: Darlene Rotchford
bio: Darlene Rotchford was elected MLA for Esquimalt-Colwood in 2024 and served as Parliamentary Secretary for Armed Forces Development and Veterans’ Affairs. She previously served as an Esquimalt councillor and as President of the Victoria Labour Council, and worked professionally in mental health and addictions.

name: Dave Johnston
bio: Dave Johnston is a Red Seal electrician who has served for the past decade as a Canadian Ranger in the Canadian Armed Forces. He founded the non-profit The North Matters in Kitimat and spent over three years managing capital projects and assets for the Haisla Nation. Born in Prince Rupert and raised in Campbell River, he lives in Colwood.

name: Sid Tobias
occupation: Mayor of View Royal; military veteran
bio: Sid Tobias has been Mayor of View Royal and a Capital Regional District director since 2022. Born in Esquimalt, he served nearly 25 years in the Canadian Armed Forces, receiving the Meritorious Service Medal, and spent more than a decade in the B.C. Public Service.

name: Sidney Coles
bio: Sidney Coles is a Victoria-based freelance journalist who has reported for outlets including Capital Daily and Canada’s National Observer, and has served as External Communications Manager for the Gitanyow Hereditary Chiefs. She previously held policy and program roles with the Ontario government and holds two PhDs from the University of Toronto.

name: Jason Leboe
bio: Jason Leboe is a utilities operator for the District of Hope and Secretary-Treasurer of the Fraser Valley Labour Council. He is a member of CUPE BC and CUPE Local 458, and lives in Hope.

name: Patrick Michell
bio: Patrick Michell is a lifelong Fraser Canyon resident who served as Chief of Kanaka Bar Indian Band from 2015 to 2022 and as Rebuild Director for Lytton First Nations from 2023 to 2025. A UBC law graduate, he practised law in Lytton from 1997 to 2005 and has served on bodies including the BC Climate Solutions Council and the Fraser Basin Council.

name: Tony Luck
bio: Tony Luck is the MLA for Fraser-Nicola and a realtor. He previously worked a decade as a financial planner and 26 years with BC Hydro, served as a Mission City councillor, and held positions with the Fraser Valley Regional District and the Southern Interior Local Government Association.

name: Dana Lajeunesse
bio: Dana Lajeunesse was elected MLA for Juan de Fuca-Malahat in 2024 and served as Parliamentary Secretary for Accessibility. A longtime Sooke resident, he holds a Mechanical Engineering Technology credential from Camosun College, worked in that industry for 24 years, and was elected to Sooke council in 2019 and 2022.

name: David Evans
bio: David Evans operates a coffee roasting business in Sooke and has been self-employed for most of the past four decades, including founding a landscaping company and a café and bakery. He holds an Applied Arts Degree from Toronto Metropolitan University and was the BC Green candidate in the riding in 2024.

name: Jeff Brown
bio: Jeff Brown is a Chartered Professional Accountant and Certified Risk Manager who has served as CEO of PL&B Insurance and American Marine Insurance. He founded the charity Sun Safe Water and lives in Sooke.

name: Mike Hicks
bio: Mike Hicks served 13 years as the elected Capital Regional District Director for the Juan de Fuca Electoral Area. A BCIT Hotel Management graduate, he has managed resorts and owned fishing lodges, and now operates a guesthouse in Sooke with his wife. He has lived in the community for 28 years.

name: Shane Friesen
bio: Shane Friesen is the OneBC candidate for Juan de Fuca-Malahat and lives in Cobble Hill. He works in the skilled trades, with experience in home site supervision, industrial inspection, and HVAC and gas fitting. He has served as Referee-in-Chief for the Kerry Park Minor Hockey Association.

name: Annelise Beach
bio: Annelise Beach is a social worker who has worked in healthcare for seven years, focusing on mental health and substance use for the past five. Raised in Burns Lake, she moved to Kamloops in 2013 to study social work at Thompson Rivers University.

name: Mike Wisla
bio: Mike Wisla is a longtime teacher and a Senior Labour Relations Officer for occupational health and safety with the Health Sciences Association. He previously worked in coal mining, pulp milling, tree planting and wildfire response, spent eight years as a paramedic, and has served 17 years as a Sea Cadet officer.

name: Peter Milobar
bio: Peter Milobar was elected MLA for Kamloops-North Thompson in 2017 and 2020 and for Kamloops Centre in 2024, and has served as Opposition House Leader and Shadow Minister for Finance. He previously served three terms as Mayor of Kamloops. He and his wife operate a local small business.

name: Rocky McAfee
bio: Rocky McAfee is the OneBC candidate for Kamloops Centre. He served as financial agent for a Kamloops-area committee that opposed the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST). He paints portraits of pets and wildlife.

name: Thaelo Proctor
bio: Thaelo Proctor is a carpenter in Kamloops who volunteers with Rotary.

name: Kory Clark
bio: Kory Clark has worked in healthcare for seven years, including as a community support worker with USW Local 1-417. A member of the Michel Band who grew up in Cache Creek and lives in Kamloops, he volunteers with Interior Health and Bonaparte First Nation.

name: Ward Stamer
bio: Ward Stamer was elected MLA for Kamloops–North Thompson in 2024 after serving as Mayor of Barriere from 2018 and on Barriere’s first municipal council from 2007. He spent about 45 years in B.C.’s forest industry and has been a member of the Barriere Lions Club for 36 years. His private member’s bill on dashboard cameras in commercial vehicles received Royal Assent in May 2026.

name: Bill Desrosiers
occupation: Business owner; equipment dealer development manager
bio: Bill Desrosiers is the OneBC candidate for Kelowna Centre. He owns an automotive repair shop in Kelowna and works as Dealer Development Manager for Western Canada with Ant Equipment Group. He lives in Upper Fintry and is a father of five.

name: Kristina Loewen
bio: Kristina Loewen is the MLA for Kelowna Centre and a real estate professional who has lived in Kelowna for 25 years. She previously worked as a care aide and doula, and has been a youth and young adult leader in her community.

name: Loyal Wooldridge
bio: Loyal Wooldridge is an entrepreneur who was elected to Kelowna city council in 2018 and 2022 and is a director and former chair of the Regional District of Central Okanagan. He volunteers with the YMCA, BC SPCA and KGH Foundation.

name: Alexandra Wright
bio: Alexandra Wright is the OneBC candidate for Kelowna-Lake Country-Coldstream. She holds a Juris Doctor from UCLA School of Law, worked as a legal advisor in the energy sector, and in 2013 co-founded a supply chain consulting firm with her husband. She runs a family farm in Ellison.

name: Binny Boparai
bio: Binny Boparai is co-founder and president of Farming Karma, a Kelowna farm-to-table beverage company, and was named Woman Entrepreneur of the Year by BC Food & Beverage in 2024. She serves on the board of the Kelowna Chamber of Commerce and on Kelowna’s Agriculture Advisory Committee, and immigrated to Canada as a teenager.

name: Carter Mochinski
bio: Carter Mochinski grew up in Lake Country and is Director of Research and Publications with the BC Youth Council. He was a delegate at the COP30 UN Climate Change Conference, serves as a youth representative with the BC Parks Foundation, and previously served as a Youth Councillor with the District of Lake Country.

name: Pavneet Singh
bio: Pavneet Singh is an entrepreneur who has built and operated multiple businesses and has lived in the Okanagan for more than 25 years. He is Vice-President of the Conservative Party of B.C. and previously served as its Director-at-Large.

name: Abraham Nordine
bio: Abraham Nordine is the OneBC candidate for Kelowna-Mission, where he grew up. He holds a business diploma from Okanagan University College and has worked as a business consultant, mortgage broker and Realtor, and now manages an import and wholesale business. He is married with five children.

name: Gavin Dew
bio: Gavin Dew is the MLA for Kelowna-Mission and the Conservative critic for Jobs, Economic Development and Innovation and AI. He previously served as Chief Strategy Officer for an agricultural innovation and food security project, holds a BA from UBC and an MBA from Oxford, and chairs the Veterans Transition Network.

name: Miriam Rycroft
bio: Miriam Rycroft has worked in public service in Ottawa and in Alberta for the Notley government, and has advocated for small businesses in the private sector.

name: Saoirse MacKinnon
bio: Saoirse MacKinnon is Department and Lab Program Manager for Earth and Environmental Sciences at UBC Okanagan, where she has worked in post-secondary education since 2015. She holds an MSc in Environmental Geosciences from the University of Victoria and two UBC bachelor’s degrees, and is a certified secondary teacher who taught math and science in B.C. and Alberta.

name: Brittny Anderson
bio: Brittny Anderson was elected MLA for Nelson-Creston in 2020 and re-elected in 2024, and has served as Minister of State for Local Governments and Rural Communities and Parliamentary Secretary for Tourism. A lifelong Kootenay resident and former small-business owner, she previously served as a Nelson city councillor and Regional District of Central Kootenay board member.

name: Gordon Skulnec
bio: Gordon Skulnec served 17 years as an RCMP general duty officer in the East Kootenays, retiring in 2023, after starting his career as a medical radiographer in Trail. He has run a rental housing and property management business for 20 years and operates a business in Salmo. He is Director of Baseball for the Cranbrook Minor Ball Association.

name: Hunter Corrigal
bio: Hunter Corrigal is the OneBC candidate for Kootenay-Central. He has worked as a BC Sheriff Service officer, a wildfire initial attack crew leader, and an equipment operator at Teck Elkview, and owns an exploration logistics and hardscape company. He has volunteered with Search & Rescue and as a Special Olympics ski coach.

name: Nicole Charlwood
bio: Nicole Charlwood served on Nelson City Council from 2021 to 2022 and has worked as a Senior Financial Officer with Elections Canada through three federal elections. She holds an honours degree in Economics and has lived in Blewett for 25 years.

name: Connie Larochelle
bio: Connie Larochelle is a retired provincial public servant who left her role as a Senior Research Advisor in Victoria in 2020. She holds an MA in Environment and Management from Royal Roads University and a Bachelor of Natural Resource Sciences from Thompson Rivers University, and lives in Trail.

name: Stephen Hill
bio: Stephen Hill is the OneBC candidate for Kootenay-Monashee and has lived in the community for 32 years. He founded the LeRoi Community Foundation in Trail and was a founding member of the Trail Youth Justice Committee. He has served on boards including Trail Hospice and Rotary.

name: Steve Morissette
bio: Steve Morissette was elected MLA for Kootenay-Monashee in 2024. He previously served as Mayor of Fruitvale, where he and his wife raised four sons.

name: Warren Mirko
bio: Warren Mirko is a public affairs consultant and a councillor in the Village of Warfield, with more than 15 years of experience in public relations and risk management for regulators including BC Financial Services Authority, Engineers and Geoscientists BC and Transport Canada. He holds a BA in Political Science from UBC.

name: AJ Wolfe
bio: AJ Wolfe is the OneBC candidate for Kootenay-Rockies. Born and raised in Fernie, he has more than 25 years of construction experience in the Kootenay region as a tradesperson, superintendent and project manager. He lives in Jaffray with his wife and three children.

name: Keenan Dennehy
bio: Keenan Dennehy is a tradesperson and wilderness guide who completed Selkirk College’s Heavy Mechanical Foundation program and has maintained machinery in remote camps. He founded the advocacy project 4theloveofbc.ca and completed training through Vancouver Island University in Indigenous Protected and Conserved Area planning.

name: Norma Blissett
occupation: City councillor; former teacher and forester
bio: Norma Blissett has served on Cranbrook City Council since 2014 and has represented Cranbrook on the Regional District of East Kootenay for the past four years. She is a former high school teacher and forester and a longtime Cranbrook resident.

name: Paul Heywood
bio: Paul Heywood has more than 27 years of experience in public service, including senior roles with the City of Cranbrook such as Director of Recreation and Culture, and as Director of the Esplanade Arts & Heritage Centre in Medicine Hat. He studied political science at the University of Victoria and is a longtime Rotary member.

name: Pete Davis
bio: Pete Davis is the MLA for Kootenay-Rockies. Originally from Revelstoke and raised in Cranbrook, he has worked as a business professional with sectors in the Elk Valley and East Kootenays including logging, forestry, automotive, heavy equipment and mining.

name: Charlene Smylie
bio: Charlene Smylie is co-founder of Redstone Electrical Services and served two terms on council in Wabamun, Alberta, first as a councillor and then as mayor. She has also served on the Alberta Municipalities Board and the Alberta Safety Codes Council, and now lives on Vancouver Island.

name: Kris McNichol
bio: Kris McNichol has ownership interests in five businesses in industrial equipment, manufacturing, construction, building products and marina operations, and has more than 25 years in business. He has lived on Vancouver Island for over 30 years, served as President of the Oceanside Minor Softball Association, and previously volunteered as a firefighter.

name: Stephanie Higginson
bio: Stephanie Higginson was elected MLA in 2024 and served as Parliamentary Secretary for Primary Care Access. She was previously elected twice to the Nanaimo-Ladysmith Board of Education and is a past president of the BC School Trustees’ Association. She has lived in the area since 2010.

name: Christian McCay
bio: Christian McCay is the Leader of the Christian Heritage Party of British Columbia. He holds three Red Seal trade certifications and a Diploma in Health and Safety and has worked in the skilled trades. He raised five children on Vancouver Island and has been involved in grassroots advocacy and community organizing.

name: Christopher Moon
bio: Christopher Moon has worked for more than nine years with the Ministry of Forests and BC Wildfire Service, currently as Provincial Payroll Lead. He holds a Diploma in Public Administration from Camosun College, was born in Victoria, and has lived in Langford since 2021.

name: Cindy Scott
bio: Cindy Scott has owned and operated KC Custom Designs Ltd., a Langford-based home building and renovation company, for more than two decades. She created The Holiday Home Tour at Bear Mountain, which raised funds for community services including the Goldstream Food Bank.

name: Ravi Parmar
bio: Ravi Parmar was elected MLA in 2023 and served as Minister of Forests. He previously served as Chair of the Sooke School Board.

name: Sean Flynn
bio: Sean Flynn served 13 years in the Royal Canadian Navy as a Naval Warfare Officer and later worked as a Senior Technical Trainer with Lockheed Martin Canada. He is CEO and a director of Avventura Resources Ltd. and COO and a director of Planet Green Metals Inc. He is a longtime Langford resident.

name: Alex Joehl
bio: Alex Joehl has been a meat department manager at a grocery store since 2012 and is a former sports writer who lives in Langley. He ran for the BC Libertarian Party in Langley-East in 2017 and 2020 and in Langley-Abbotsford in 2024, and has run four times federally for the Libertarian Party of Canada, most recently in Langley Township-Fraser Heights in 2025. He finished third in the 2018 Township of Langley mayoral race and ran for school board in 2021 and council in 2022.

name: Erin Osborne
bio: Erin Osborne grew up in a military family. She worked as a manager at The Book Man, an independent shop in the Fraser Valley, and as a public servant has worked on issues including reconciliation.

name: Harman Bhangu
bio: Harman Bhangu is the MLA for Langley-Abbotsford, first elected in 2024, and serves as the BC Conservative Shadow Minister for Transportation. He was elected Vice-President of the Conservative Party of BC in 2022, served as its Regional Director for Surrey, and was the party's candidate in the 2022 Surrey South by-election. His family has roots in trucking, construction and forestry.

name: Melissa Snazell
bio: Melissa Snazell is a Registered Pharmacy Technician with more than 25 years of experience in healthcare, including veterinary, community pharmacy and hospital pharmacy settings. She is completing a Bachelor of Arts at Kwantlen Polytechnic University in Applied Geography and Philosophy with a minor in Policy Studies, and serves as the BC Greens' Fraser Valley Regional Representative.

name: Shelly Jan
bio: Shelly Jan is the OneBC candidate for Langley-Abbotsford. She holds a Bachelor of Science, a Bachelor of Education and a Master of Education, began her career as a teacher, and spent 19 years working with a teachers' union. She has organized humanitarian trips for more than a decade.

name: Holly Isaac
bio: Holly Isaac was born in Surrey and raised in Langley, and her family has lived in North Langley for more than 33 years. She is 1st Vice-President of the local executive of the Canadian Union of Postal Workers, where she served as local media contact during a strike, and has served on the union's regional disciplinary committee.

name: Kyle Stevenson
bio: Kyle Stevenson is a Langley-raised former journeyman electrician who lives in Walnut Grove. He entered the trades in 2006, working on industrial projects in natural gas, mining and solar, and most recently at Tesla Energy. He has since earned a commercial pilot licence and is working toward a flight instructor rating.

name: Misty Van Popta
bio: Misty Van Popta is a Langley native and the MLA for Langley-Walnut Grove, elected in 2024. She was elected to Township of Langley council in 2022 and has served on Metro Vancouver's Water and Climate Action committees. She is a construction project management professional with a PMP designation, educated at SFU, and previously owned a small business and worked in pharmaceutical software.

name: Sam Meyer
bio: Sam Meyer grew up in Walnut Grove and studied philosophy and orchestral trumpet performance at the University of British Columbia. He works with a Vancouver-based international broadcasting company, performs professionally as a musician with local orchestras and productions, and has eight years of experience teaching violin and trumpet.

name: Andrew Mercier
bio: Andrew Mercier is a labour lawyer, former legal counsel for Teamsters Local No. 213 and former Executive Director of the BC Building Trades. He was first elected as MLA for Langley in 2020 and served as Minister of State for Sustainable Forestry Innovation. In 2026 he became Chief of Staff to Premier David Eby.

name: Anisha Sandhu
bio: Anisha Sandhu is a community food security coordinator born and raised in British Columbia. She previously chaired Seeds of Change Surrey, sat on Surrey's Agricultural and Food Policy Committee, and served as a UBC Senator and Alma Mater Society executive. She holds a Master of Science in Human Nutrition and a Bachelor of Science in Food, Nutrition and Health from UBC.

name: Jody Toor
bio: Jody Toor was born in Langley and is the MLA for Langley-Willowbrook. She runs an integrative holistic clinic in Langley and holds doctorates in Integrative Medicine and Humanitarian Services from the Board of Integrative Medicine; she is non-prescribing and not registered with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of BC. She is a breast cancer survivor and has volunteered with local food banks and charities.

name: Shubham Joshi
bio: Shubham Joshi is the OneBC candidate for Langley-Willowbrook. He is a registered physiotherapist and a Clinical Instructor in UBC's Faculty of Medicine, teaching in the Master of Physical Therapy program, and has worked as a National Team Physiotherapist. He speaks English, Hindi, Gujarati and Punjabi.

name: Daniel Kite
bio: Daniel Kite is a public school teacher in School District 42, teaching Social Studies, English and Student Leadership. He holds a BA (Honours) and a Bachelor of Education from the University of Toronto, taught internationally for seven years in China, Egypt and Russia, and is a staff representative with the Maple Ridge Teachers' Association. He has lived in Maple Ridge since 2023.

name: Hudson Campbell
bio: Hudson Campbell is a School Trustee for School District 42. He was a founding member of UPlan with the City of Maple Ridge, served as President of the Maple Ridge Climate Hub, was Director of Protocol for the 2024 BC Summer Games, and chaired the District Student Advisory Council.

name: Lawrence Mok
bio: Lawrence Mok was elected MLA for Maple Ridge East in 2024. He moved to Canada from Singapore in 1988 and has lived in Maple Ridge for over 30 years. He has more than 30 years of experience in the overhead crane and hoist industry, holds nine degrees including engineering, business and theology degrees, and volunteers with the Maple Ridge Salvation Army Church.

name: Doug Morneau
bio: Doug Morneau has lived in Maple Ridge for eight years and has four decades of business experience, currently advising companies on technology spending. He served on the board of BC Assessment and has been a director of Crossroads Hospice Society, a Chamber of Commerce and a Rotary Club. He leads programs at Maple Ridge Community Church.

name: Jordan Simmons
bio: Jordan Simmons is co-founder and CEO of Nominee, a technology platform and social enterprise providing governance and political leadership training. He previously served as a senior advisor to several BC cabinet ministers and has served on the boards of Cuso International, the Immigrant Services Society of BC and the Canadian Black Policy Network. He has lived in west Maple Ridge for seven years.

name: Lisa Beare
bio: Lisa Beare began in politics in 2014 as a school board trustee. She was elected MLA in 2017, 2020 and 2024 and has served as a Cabinet Minister with portfolios including tourism, culture, sport and post-secondary education.

name: Susan Einarsson
bio: Susan Einarsson is the OneBC candidate for Maple Ridge-Pitt Meadows. She worked for 25 years as a news anchor and reporter, including at CKNW and News 1130, and taught at BCIT for more than a decade. She owns My Town Maple Ridge News Society, a local news organization.

name: Gracie MacDonald
bio: Gracie MacDonald is Executive Director of a community school society on Denman Island and serves on the board of a nonprofit affordable housing organization there. She has worked as an elementary school principal and K-12 teacher on Vancouver Island, and earlier as a journalist and partner in an organic food business. She holds a Master of Education from the University of Victoria and an undergraduate degree from Concordia University.

name: Joshua Dahling
bio: Joshua Dahling was born in Johannesburg and came to Canada in 1980. He studied human services in Nanaimo, worked in alcohol and drug treatment facilities, and in 2009 co-founded LUMARA, a registered charity supporting families affected by serious illness and bereavement. He has lived in Port Alberni since 2018.

name: Josie Osborne
bio: Josie Osborne is Minister of Finance and was elected MLA for Mid Island-Pacific Rim in 2020 and 2024, serving in portfolios including Energy, Mines and Low Carbon Innovation and Health. A Tofino resident for over 25 years, she worked as a fisheries biologist for the Nuu-chah-nulth Tribal Council, led an environmental education non-profit, and was mayor of Tofino for almost eight years.

name: Anna Mary McKenzie
bio: Anna Mary McKenzie is a Cree journalist and policy advisor and a member of Opaskwayak Cree Nation. She began her career as a youth worker, is an advisor with Spotlight: Child Welfare, and received a Jack Webster Award for her reporting. She holds a BA in First Nations and Indigenous Studies from UBC and serves on the board of tâpwêwin media.

name: Mark MacDonald
bio: Mark MacDonald has run publishing and communications companies for more than 20 years, including the Business Examiner and Communication Ink Media & Public Relations Ltd., and was Managing Editor of the Nanaimo Daily News. He is a past President of the Greater Nanaimo Chamber of Commerce, current President of the Vancouver Island Junior Hockey League, and author of a book on small business.

name: Sheila Malcolmson
bio: Sheila Malcolmson is the incumbent MLA for Nanaimo-Gabriola Island and has been elected four times.

name: George Anderson
bio: George Anderson was born and raised in Nanaimo and was elected MLA for Nanaimo-Lantzville in 2024, serving as Parliamentary Secretary for Climate and Energy Solutions and earlier for Transit. He was previously a commercial lawyer and the youngest person elected to Nanaimo City Council, and has chaired the Vancouver Island University Board of Governors. He received the BC Achievement Award in 2016.

name: Kelsey Pringle
bio: Kelsey Pringle is co-founder and owner of Motivation Monday Marketing, a digital marketing agency, and co-founded Empower Women Canada. She sits on the Board of the Vancouver Island Economic Alliance and lived in the Nanaimo-Lantzville area for 12 years.

name: Pepper Saltman
bio: Pepper Saltman holds an economics degree from UNBC and an accounting diploma and computer science degree from Vancouver Island University. She worked for 15 years in food service and hospital housekeeping and has volunteered with the Communist Party since 2019.

name: Sharleen Weatherley
bio: Sharleen Weatherley is a high school teacher on Vancouver Island and a former data scientist in Toronto. She holds a degree in Chemical Engineering and Bioengineering, a Master's degree in Statistics and a Bachelor of Education. In BC she has worked as a whitewater rafting guide in Squamish and a whitewater safety technician in Hope.

name: Diane Black
bio: Diane Black is a third-generation rancher and a Chartered Professional Accountant with an MBA. She has worked in the agriculture, energy, logging, transportation and advanced education sectors, including as Associate Vice President Finance at Nicola Valley Institute of Technology.

name: Jesse Gervais
bio: Jesse Gervais works for the Municipality of Fraser Lake and serves on the boards of UNBC and the Fraser Lake Community Foundation. He has worked in economic development.

name: Jennifer Whiteside
bio: Jennifer Whiteside was born and raised in New Westminster and is a former labour leader who led BC's first living wage campaign. She was elected MLA for New Westminster in October 2020 and re-elected in 2024. She is Minister of Labour and previously served as Minister of Mental Health and Addictions and Minister of Education and Child Care.

name: Maureen Curran
bio: Maureen Curran has taught Science and Mathematics in Coquitlam for 25 years and spent four years with Simon Fraser University's teacher education program. She holds a BSc from McGill University and a Master's in Physics from the University of Victoria, and conducted nuclear physics research at TRIUMF. She helped create the Climate Safe Cities Coalition.

name: Michele Lau
bio: Michele Lau is a financial services executive and entrepreneur with more than 20 years of experience in banking, corporate finance and private business, including ventures in hospitality, real estate and investment management. She co-founded the World Trade Centre Okanagan and holds a Bachelor of Commerce from UBC and an Executive MBA from Simon Fraser University.

name: Francis Racy
bio: Francis Racy was born and raised in northern BC and is of Tsimshian and Gitxsan descent, holding the hereditary name En nuu Ann Gaiwh. Since February 2026 she has led mental health education programming across the North Coast region, and she has worked as a Health Care Assistant and Early Childhood Educator. She is a founding board member of the Wilp Sustainability Forum and is completing a Bachelor of General Studies at Thompson Rivers University.

name: Rodney Proskiw
bio: Rodney Proskiw has lived in Prince Rupert for 20 years. He is a small business owner and longtime union member with UFCW 1518, UFCW 247 and the Teamsters. He is a past President of the Prince Rupert Lions Club and retired as the longest-serving director on the board of Tourism Prince Rupert.

name: Tamara Davidson
bio: Tamara Davidson (Haida name Laanas) was first elected in 2024 and served as Minister of Environment and Parks. She previously served on the Council of the Haida Nation, was a member of the Haida Negotiations Support Team, and worked as a federal public servant.

name: Anna Kindy
bio: Anna Kindy is a physician and addiction medicine specialist and the MLA for North Island. She graduated from the University of Alberta Medical School in 1986, practised in remote Quebec and Port Hardy, and has worked in Campbell River since 1998. She represented Canada in mogul skiing at the 1992 Albertville Olympics.

name: Benjamin Olsson
bio: Benjamin Olsson is a Registered Social Worker who has lived in Campbell River since 2010. He holds a Bachelor of Social Work from the University of Regina and a post-degree diploma in mental health and addiction from Camosun College. He has more than two decades of union activism and was Leader of the Green Party of Saskatchewan in 2003.

name: Sara Lopez
bio: Sara Lopez has lived in Campbell River for more than a decade. She is a former Executive Director of the Campbell River Art Gallery and works with Habitat for Humanity Vancouver Island North.

name: Bowinn Ma
bio: Bowinn Ma is a professional engineer elected MLA in 2017, 2020 and 2024. She has served as Minister of Emergency Management and Climate Readiness and Minister of Infrastructure.

name: Joshua A Singer Johnson
bio: Joshua A. Singer Johnson is a lawyer and lifelong North Vancouver resident whose work has included constitutional and Indigenous litigation, international human rights and tenant advocacy. He studied History and Philosophy at the University of Ottawa and earned his law degree at McGill University.

name: Trevor Withers
bio: Trevor Withers is a North Shore resident and Queen's University graduate who works as a Data Visualization Engineer at Aritzia. He previously worked at Tap & Barrel in North Vancouver, played junior hockey with the North Vancouver Wolfpack and has refereed local minor hockey.

name: Ben Holt
bio: Ben Holt was raised in North Vancouver-Seymour and works in technology as a software development team lead and systems administrator. He holds a Bachelor's degree in Political Science from the University of Victoria, has chaired the Mount Fromme Residents Association, and has coached youth soccer and baseball.

name: Lori Climenhaga
bio: Lori Climenhaga has lived in Deep Cove for more than 16 years and runs a consulting practice focused on community engagement and workforce development. She previously worked at WCG International, was Director of Member Relations at the BC Chamber of Commerce, and from 2020 was a Director with the BC government. She has served on the boards of the North Vancouver Chamber and the BC Chamber Executives Society.

name: Lynne Block
bio: Lynne Block is an educator and former West Vancouver school trustee who was elected MLA in 2024. She holds a Bachelor's degree and a Master of Education from UBC, received the Prime Minister's Award for Teaching Excellence, and co-founded a business and education consulting company.

name: Susie Chant
bio: Susie Chant was raised on the North Shore and has lived in Lynn Valley since 1988. She is the MLA for North Vancouver-Seymour and has worked as a Registered Nurse and served in the Royal Canadian Navy Reserves.

name: Andrew Appleton
bio: Andrew Appleton is a two-term District of Oak Bay councillor and has more than 25 years of experience in environmental protection and conservation. He represented Oak Bay on the Greater Victoria Library Board, serving as Board Chair in 2023-24, and chaired the District's Community Climate Action Working Group.

name: Andrew Weaver
bio: Andrew Weaver is a Professor in the School of Earth and Ocean Sciences at the University of Victoria and a former Canada Research Chair in Climate Modelling. He was elected BC Green Party MLA for Oak Bay-Gordon Head in 2013, led the BC Green Party from 2015, and served two terms. He holds a PhD in Applied Mathematics from UBC and was appointed to the Order of British Columbia in 2008.

name: Diana Gibson
bio: Diana Gibson was elected MLA for Oak Bay-Gordon Head in 2024 and served as Minister of Citizens' Services and earlier Minister of Jobs, Economic Development and Innovation. She previously led Greater Victoria's Community Social Planning Council and co-founded the Firelight Group, an Indigenous-owned consulting firm.

name: Stan Sipos
bio: Stan Sipos came to Canada as a refugee from Yugoslavia. After a decade in the construction trades, he has worked more than 50 years in business and real estate development in BC, including the Customs House heritage revitalization in Victoria, and co-founded Cielo Carbon Solutions. He is an inductee of the Canadian Drag Racing Hall of Fame and lives in Oak Bay.

name: Curtis Whitford
bio: Curtis Whitford lives in Fort St. John and has 36 years of experience in the oil and gas industry, including field operations, gas plant operations, oilfield waste management and as regional manager with an oilfield engineering firm. He completed Fourth Class Power Engineering training at SAIT and has volunteered with minor hockey as a coach and board member.

name: Jordan Kealy
bio: Jordan Kealy is a farmer who was elected MLA for Peace River North in 2024 as a BC Conservative. He left the Conservative Party in March 2025 and has since sat as an independent.

name: Larry Neufeld
bio: Larry Neufeld is a Professional Engineer and the MLA for Peace River South. He holds a Bachelor of Applied Science in Engineering, was a vice president of an environmental remediation contractor, and has founded and managed his own companies since 2006. He is a former Reserve Infantry Platoon Commander.

name: Marsha Rose Dufresne
bio: Marsha Rose Dufresne is a longtime Indigenous Education Support Worker. She has served as a director with Tumbler Ridge Community Forests and the Tumbler Ridge UNESCO Global Geopark, and is a community volunteer.

name: Bradley Sean Bartsch
bio: Bradley Sean Bartsch has worked with organizations including Ronald McDonald House BC & Yukon, World Vision Canada, Simon Fraser University and RBC Financial Group, including fundraising for healthcare and social housing. He holds a BA in Political Science and Business Administration from SFU, moved to Penticton in 2021, and sits on the board of the Penticton Academy of Music and Dramatic Arts.

name: Tina Lee
bio: Tina Lee is a Penticton resident raising two children. She is a member of the Okanagan College Board of Governors and volunteers with local organizations including Penticton Safety Village, the Community Foundation of the South Okanagan and Dragonfly Pond.

name: Tracy St Claire
bio: Tracy St. Claire grew up in Penticton and has spent 14 years with the South Okanagan Similkameen Division of Family Practice, nine as Executive Director. She previously worked in negotiation and mediation, including with the BC Treaty Commission, and served as Vice-Chair and Finance Chair of the Okanagan Skaha School Board. She holds an MA from Simon Fraser University and a BA from UBC.

name: Warren Hamm
bio: Warren Hamm is the OneBC candidate for Penticton-Summerland. He is a contractor, licensed aircraft maintenance engineer and small-business owner with more than 30 years of experience in aviation, construction, resources and emergency response. He was the first declared candidate in the 2026 BC Conservative leadership race before joining OneBC.

name: Keenan Adams
bio: Keenan Adams has lived in Port Coquitlam since 2010, when he graduated from BCIT's Railway Conductor program; he advanced from conductor to locomotive engineer and now helps train railway workers. He is Local President of Teamsters Canada Rail Conference Local 320 and volunteers with the PoCo Lions Club.

name: Lewis C. Dahlby
bio: Lewis Dahlby was born in Chilliwack, lives in Port Coquitlam and runs a trucking and excavating business. He first ran for office in 1988 for the federal Libertarian Party.

name: Mike Farnworth
bio: Mike Farnworth has lived in Port Coquitlam for more than 50 years. He served three terms as a Port Coquitlam city councillor before being elected MLA in 1991, and has been re-elected six times. He has held several senior cabinet positions, most recently Minister of Transportation.

name: Stephanie Hendy
bio: Stephanie Hendy has more than 17 years of experience in health, rehabilitation and accessibility-related fields, most recently in third-party disability management. She holds a BSc in Kinesiology and a certificate as a Clinical Exercise Physiologist, chaired the Okanagan Transit Alliance in 2024, and served on the City of Vernon Climate Advisory Committee. She ran for the BC Greens in Vancouver-Langara in 2020.

name: Freddy Rawji
bio: Freddy Rawji was born and raised in Port Moody and holds a BSc in Economics from the University of Victoria. He worked at RAM Consulting from 2018 and in 2020 founded Torus Talent, a recruitment and leadership consulting firm specializing in technical talent.

name: John McEwen
bio: John McEwen has lived in Anmore for more than 20 years and served 18 years on Anmore Council, including 12 as Mayor. He has served as Vice Chair of the Metro Vancouver Board, chaired its Parks Committee, sat on the Mayors' Council on TransLink, and is a trustee with the Municipal Finance Authority of BC. He founded and sold two small businesses.

name: Rick Glumac
bio: Rick Glumac is a three-term MLA who has served as Minister of State for AI and New Technologies, Minister of State for Trade, and Parliamentary Secretary for Technology. A former Port Moody city councillor and past President of the Pacific NorthWest Economic Region, he previously worked in computer animation and video games. He has lived in Port Moody for more than 20 years.

name: Wei Chou
bio: Wei Chou grew up in Port Moody after coming to Canada in 1997. In 2019 he founded a Vancouver-based technology startup, which he later wound down, and has worked in supply chain management and with Local 40, the hotel workers' union. He mentors entrepreneurs and researchers through Innovation UBC, Lab2Market and New Ventures BC.

name: Griffin Leonard Lea
occupation: Canada Post letter carrier; theatre producer
bio: Griffin Leonard Lea has worked as a Canada Post letter carrier for nine years and co-founded a theatre production company. Born and raised on Vancouver Island, he holds a diploma in film production from the Pacific Film & New Media Academy and worked as an Elections Officer in New Zealand's 2011 election.

name: John Henderson
bio: John Henderson is in his second term as Mayor of the District of Sechelt, re-elected in 2022. He has chaired the Sunshine Coast Community Forest and served on the BC Ferries board from 2004 to 2008. He holds a Bachelor of Commerce from UBC and is a Chartered Accountant, with nearly 50 years of business experience including 20 years in Hong Kong.

name: Randene Neill
bio: Randene Neill was elected MLA for Powell River-Sunshine Coast in 2024 and served as Minister of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship. She previously worked as a reporter and anchor at Global BC for nearly two decades and as a communications consultant.

name: Ian McMahon
bio: Ian McMahon has three decades of experience in provincial, federal and international politics, including roles in the B.C. government, on Parliament Hill and at the Canadian Embassy in Washington, D.C. He has worked on B.C. forestry issues, taught political science, and managed campaigns and government relations work.

name: Kiel Giddens
occupation: MLA; former LNG industry relations professional
bio: Kiel Giddens is a Prince George resident who spent over a decade working on the development of B.C.'s LNG industry. He is a past president of the Prince George Chamber of Commerce and serves on the board of the Spirit of the North Healthcare Foundation. He previously served as chief of staff to B.C.'s Minister of Environment and to the Minister of Transportation and Infrastructure.

name: Teri Young
bio: Teri Young holds a Bachelor of Education from UBC and taught in Gitlax̱t'aamiks (New Aiyansh) in Nisga'a territory. She founded and ran Paxar Technologies Corp, a national software distribution company, for more than 30 years before retiring in 2018. She lives in Cowichan Bay, volunteers with Cowichan Hospice and is a member of the Koksilah Watershed Working Group.

name: Denice Bardua
bio: Denice Bardua has lived in Quesnel since 1997 and works in education. She is a member of the Bouchie Lake community and of her union.

name: Randy Thompson
bio: Randy Thompson co-owns the Oddball Garlic Company with his wife and moved to Quesnel about 20 years ago. He drove truck for Arrow Transport for 10 years and now works for the City of Quesnel. He served two years on the BC Green Party's Provincial Council and was the party's candidate in Prince George-North Cariboo in 2024.

name: Sheldon Clare
bio: Sheldon Clare was born in Prince George and has taught at the College of New Caledonia since 1993, where he also served as a contract negotiator and on the Board of Governors. He holds a BA from UBC and an MA from Norwich University, and is a former reserve army officer. He was national president of the National Firearms Association from 2010 to 2021 and is a past president of Royal Canadian Legion Branch 43.

name: Carol Bourque
bio: Carol Bourque was born and raised in Prince George and has over 30 years of public-sector service, including 14 years in Health Information Management with Northern Health. She is Indigenous and brought the Tampon Tuesday campaign to Prince George in 2018.

name: Jodie Capling
bio: Jodie Capling grew up in the Cariboo-Chilcotin and holds a Master's degree in Resource and Environmental Management, after which she worked five years in energy efficiency. She lives in Williams Lake, teaches yoga and movement, and is a member of the Williams Lake Climate Change Circle. She ran as a Green Party candidate in the 2026 federal election.

name: Mitchell Lukoni
bio: Mitchell Lukoni is the OneBC candidate for Prince George-Valemount, where he was born and raised. He holds a Bachelor of General Studies from Athabasca University and works as a business, communications and policy strategist. He has volunteered with the Prince George Hospice Palliative Care Society.

name: Rosalyn Bird
bio: Rosalyn Bird was elected MLA for Prince George-Valemount in November 2024 and served as Official Opposition Whip, with critic roles including Citizens' Services and Children and Family Development. She sponsored the Veterans and First Responders Act in 2026. She served more than 20 years in the Canadian Armed Forces, commissioned as a Naval Logistics Officer in 2005.

name: Linda Li
bio: Linda Li has lived in Richmond since 1996 and is the managing broker at Selmak Realty Ltd. She has been involved with the Richmond Chinese Community Society and the Richmond Hospital Foundation.

name: Teresa Wat
bio: Teresa Wat was first elected MLA for Richmond Centre in 2013 and was re-elected in Richmond-Bridgeport in 2024. From 2013 to 2017 she was Minister of International Trade and Minister Responsible for the Asia Pacific Strategy and Multiculturalism. She was previously News Director at Channel M Television and President and CEO of Mainstream Broadcasting Corporation.

name: Calvin Dang
bio: Calvin Dang has operated federally registered seafood and meat processing businesses in Richmond since 2014. He has helped lead a nonprofit Asian Canadian basketball organization in Richmond for more than five years and is a board member of the Canadian Community Service Association. He holds a Bachelor's degree in Economics from the University of Manitoba.

name: Henry Yao
bio: Henry Yao was born in Taiwan and moved to Richmond when he was young. He served as MLA for Richmond South Centre from 2020 to 2024 and has volunteered with several community organizations.

name: Sacha Peter
bio: Sacha Peter is a Chartered Professional Accountant specializing in corporate taxation, born and raised in Richmond, with a BSc in Physics from UBC. He has written about finance and investing at Divestor.com since 2009 and hosts the Late Night Finance show. He was twice elected to the Cultus Lake Park Board, serving six years including three as Chair.

name: Dhar Grewal
bio: Dhar Grewal was born in Campbell River and has lived in Richmond for three decades. He is a Senior Manager at Vancity, has coached local youth soccer, and has supported organizations such as the ALS Society.

name: Luc Burns
bio: Luc Burns is a materials engineer and quality assurance professional who works in Richmond, with five years of experience in quality assurance and manufacturing. He holds a BASc in Materials Engineering from UBC, serves as a union job steward, and is secretary of his strata council.

name: Steve Kooner
bio: Steve Kooner is a lawyer who has owned Steve Kooner Law Corporation for over 17 years, practising in litigation. He holds a BA in Political Science from Simon Fraser University and a JD from the University of Calgary. Born in Vancouver, he received the Queen's Platinum Jubilee Award in 2023.

name: Barry Wosk
bio: Barry Wosk is a lifelong Richmond resident who holds a Bachelor of Commerce from UBC and has operated a Richmond-based small business for more than three decades. He has volunteered with the Steveston High School Alumni Association, Big Brothers and RCM-SAR, and served as a director of the Richmond Chamber of Commerce.

name: Bruce Kong
bio: Bruce Kong owns an auto body shop in Richmond. He is a father of two.

name: Gordon Zhang
bio: Gordon Zhang has taught business at Kwantlen Polytechnic University's Richmond campus for more than 17 years. He has co-founded several companies, including helping establish an N95 respirator production line in Richmond and a laboratory accredited to test respirators and medical masks. He has fundraised for the Richmond Hospital Foundation through the local Lions Club.

name: Emily Lowan
occupation: Leader of the BC Greens; climate organizer
bio: Emily Lowan is the leader of the BC Greens and grew up on the Saanich Peninsula. She has worked as fossil fuel supply campaigns lead for Climate Action Network Canada and as an investigative researcher with the Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives' Corporate Mapping Project.

name: Kala Bryson
bio: Kala Bryson is a lawyer and community advocate who was raised in co-op housing. She earned her JD from the University of Victoria.

name: Richard Smith
bio: Dr. Richard Smith is a research scientist in immunology and microbiology with a PhD from UBC, and has managed life-science projects for Defence R&D Canada and the Canadian Forces Health Services Group. He served as a contact tracer and case manager with Island Health during COVID-19 and has been president of Royal Canadian SAR (Sidney).

name: Ryan Windsor
bio: Ryan Windsor was first elected to Central Saanich council in a 2013 by-election and has served as Mayor since 2014, returned by acclamation in 2018 and 2022. He has served as a director on the Capital Regional District board and previously worked in the private sector and his family's business.

name: Cathie Ounsted
bio: Cathie Ounsted co-operates the accounting firm Ounsted and Company and has lived and worked in Saanich South for over 35 years. She has served on Central Saanich Council, the Central Saanich Police Board and the Peninsula Co-Op board, and spent nine years on the Victoria Airport Authority board, the last two as Chair. She previously owned the Red Barn Market and was Director of Operations for Thrifty Foods.

name: Lisa Lapointe
bio: Lisa Lapointe served as British Columbia's Chief Coroner from 2011 until her retirement in 2024, having joined the BC Public Service in 1995. She holds a law degree from UBC and has chaired the Canadian Forum of Chief Coroners and Chief Medical Examiners. She is a board member of PHS Community Services Society.

name: Richard Zussman
bio: Richard Zussman is a journalist who worked as a legislative reporter for Global BC and CBC and served as President of the B.C. Legislative Press Gallery. He serves on the boards of the Lakehill Baseball and Fastball Association and the Victoria Curling Club, and has lived on the South Island for more than a decade.

name: Barbara Presch
bio: Barbara Presch is the OneBC candidate for Salmon Arm-Shuswap, where her family settled in 1982. She holds a business diploma from SAIT and Respiratory Therapy credentials and a Bachelor of Health Sciences from Thompson Rivers University. She has worked in health care for 24 years.

name: David L Williams
occupation: MLA; insurance loss control specialist and appraiser
bio: David L. Williams is a Shuswap resident who has worked in the HVAC industry, real estate, with the B.C. Assessment Authority and as a regional appraiser in Saskatchewan, and currently as a loss control specialist and residential appraiser in insurance. He has served as a board director of the Kelowna Metis Community Services Society and chaired the CSRD Board of Variance.

name: Denise Reimer
bio: Denise Reimer has more than 30 years with BC Emergency Health Services, including as a Primary Care Paramedic, Emergency Medical Dispatcher and Critical Care Coordinator. She served as a Salmon Arm city councillor and Deputy Mayor, and deployed with Canadian Medical Assistance Teams to Pakistan in 2010 and the Philippines in 2013. She received the Governor General's EMS Exemplary Service Medal in 2025.

name: Gloria Morgan
bio: Gloria Morgan is a member and former Chief of the Splatsin First Nation. She served 11 years as an RCMP officer before being called to the bar in 1995, and has worked in private practice, as Crown Counsel and as a Federal Adjudicator in the Indian Residential School Independent Assessment Process.

name: Jed Wiebe
bio: Jed Wiebe is a lifelong Shuswap resident who co-owns and operates Elderberry Grove, an organic elderberry farm in Salmon Arm. He has a background in sociology and anthropology and experience in silviculture, and sits on the City of Salmon Arm's Environmental Advisory Committee. He was the BC Greens candidate in Salmon Arm-Shuswap in 2024.

name: Claire Rattée
bio: Claire Rattée was born and raised in Delta and moved to Kitimat in 2011. She has owned a business for 13 years and served four years on Kitimat City Council. She was the Conservative candidate in the 2019 and 2021 federal elections.

name: Larry Eugene Taylor
bio: Larry Eugene Taylor, listed by OneBC as Larry Taylor, is the party's candidate for Skeena. Born and raised in Terrace, he has worked as a heavy duty mechanic for over 42 years and was a volunteer firefighter in Terrace for 13 years.

name: Nick Gottlieb
bio: Nick Gottlieb is a writer, researcher and PhD candidate at Simon Fraser University studying the political economy of Canada's LNG industry, and received a Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship in 2025. He has lived in Terrace for five years, helped establish the Skeena Local Action Network, and serves on the board of BC Whitewater.

name: Sarah Zimmerman
bio: Sarah Zimmerman is a Terrace city councillor, former journalist and communications professional. She volunteers with organizations including the Terrace Rotary Club and My Mountain Co-op.

name: Amna Shah
bio: Amna Shah was first elected MLA for Surrey-City Centre in 2024 and was appointed Deputy Government Whip and Parliamentary Secretary for Mental Health and Addictions and for Anti-Racism Initiatives. She has served on the Surrey Food Bank board, previously worked with B.C.'s Ministry of Housing, and has lived in Surrey for nearly 20 years.

name: Oliver Wildfong
bio: Oliver Wildfong is the OneBC candidate for Surrey City Centre and has lived in Surrey since 2005. He holds a BCIT diploma in security systems and since 2019 has co-owned a Lower Mainland security firm. He is a certified Security Systems Technician.

name: Raman Sharma
occupation: Entrepreneur; President, Tradesman Association of BC
bio: Raman Sharma is a Surrey resident who arrived in Canada in 1998. He founded the Tradesman Association of BC in 2016 and serves as its President, and founded the Annual Construction Expo and the South Asian Construction Excellence (SACE) Awards. He has volunteered with Lakshmi Narayan Hindu Temple for over 22 years and is a Director with Unite to Help.

name: Zeeshan Wahla
bio: Zeeshan Wahla is a Professional Engineer who runs his own engineering consulting firm and is registered as a P.Eng. in four provinces. He immigrated to British Columbia in 2007 and has lived in Surrey since. He and his wife are raising four daughters in Surrey.

name: Nicholas Cartmell
occupation: Brand strategist; former CEO, BC Sports Hall of Fame and Museum
bio: Nicholas Cartmell is a brand strategist and former CEO of the BC Sports Hall of Fame and Museum who has lived in Surrey since 2012. He spent 14 years at TELUS, most recently as Senior Director, Strategic Initiatives, Partnerships and Government Relations. He served on Capilano University's Board of Governors from 2016 to 2018 and is Vice President of the Surrey 2027 55+ BC Games Host Society.

name: Pat McCutcheon
bio: Pat McCutcheon is a retired professional engineer and longtime Cloverdale resident with a Bachelor of Applied Science from the University of British Columbia. He founded an engineering consulting firm in 1995 serving heavy equipment manufacturers and operated it for 28 years. He is a member of the Cloverdale District Chamber of Commerce and volunteers with local nonprofit organizations.

name: Sargy Chima
bio: Sargy Chima is a Team Leader with Service Canada with more than 20 years of public service experience, and a Surrey resident of nearly 40 years. She previously served as an elected National Executive Vice President of her union and has volunteered with Cloverdale Minor Hockey. She has previously run for provincial office in Surrey-Whalley and for Surrey City Council.

name: Stephen Dooley
bio: Stephen Dooley is the retired Executive Director of Simon Fraser University's Surrey campus and previously taught criminology and sociology at Kwantlen Polytechnic University, where he was its first Director of Community Engagement. He is a former Director and Chair of the Surrey Board of Trade and Co-Chair of the Surrey Poverty Reduction Coalition. He holds a Master's degree in Sociology and has lived in the region for over 25 years.

name: Travis Marchenski
bio: Travis Marchenski is the OneBC candidate for Surrey-Cloverdale. He worked for over a decade on construction sites before founding his own small construction business. He lives in Surrey with his wife and child.

name: Carolyn Hofbauer
bio: Carolyn Hofbauer is the OneBC candidate for Surrey-Fleetwood and grew up in Surrey's Newton neighbourhood. She worked as a chef, including nearly a decade as head chef at The Vault Restaurant in Cloverdale, and now manages BC Firearms Academy with her husband.

name: Garry Purewal
bio: Garry Purewal is a business owner who served as a Military Police member with the Canadian Armed Forces. He has owned and managed companies including a property restoration business, and has been a leader in youth sports.

name: Jagrup Brar
bio: Jagrup Brar is the incumbent MLA for Surrey-Fleetwood. He is the past Executive Director of the Surrey Self Employment and Entrepreneur Development Society (SEEDS), where he trained new entrepreneurs. He lives in Surrey with his wife and two children.

name: Paul Brar
bio: Paul Brar came to Canada in 1983, first working as a shingle sawyer in Mission, and built a career in real estate over the following four decades. He earned a diploma in Urban Land Economics from the University of British Columbia in 1999 and previously attended DAV College and Punjab Agricultural University. He has volunteered on municipal, provincial and federal campaigns and raised four children in Surrey.

name: Tim Binnema
bio: Tim Binnema has spent more than 25 years in senior leadership with a British Columbia-based engineering and equipment supply company focused on pollution-control and energy-optimization systems. He has lived in Fleetwood since 2000, where he and his wife raised four children.

name: Garry Begg
bio: Garry Begg was first elected as MLA for Surrey-Guildford in 2017 and was appointed Parliamentary Secretary for Surrey Infrastructure in July 2025; he previously served as Minister of Public Safety and Solicitor General and as Government Whip. Before his election he spent over 38 years as an RCMP officer, the last eight in Surrey, including as a District Commander.

name: Garry Thind
bio: Garry Thind is a Realtor with Century 21 Coastal Realty and has served as a Trustee on the Surrey School Board for 12 years, currently as Vice-Chair. He is a past President of the Rotary Club of Surrey and leads the BC region for the Pingalwara Society of Ontario. He has lived in Surrey for more than 27 years.

name: Jodi Murphy
bio: Jodi Murphy is an operations manager who spent a decade managing technical services for BC's pulp and paper industry and later worked with biotechnology start-ups; she has since started a small business in Surrey and worked in an accounting role for the Province.
