She holds a Bachelor of Science from UBC. She was the BC Green candidate in Surrey-Guildford in 2017 and 2020 and has lived in the riding for almost 15 years.

name: Harj Dhaliwal
bio: Harj Dhaliwal is a business executive and educator who holds an MBA and a PhD in Organization Development and Leadership and has taught undergraduate and graduate business courses. He served six years as a Director of TransLink and four years on the board of the BC SPCA, and has chaired the Surrey Metro Soccer Association. He has lived in Surrey for 28 years.

name: Harman Preet Singh
bio: Harman Preet Singh is completing his legal articling in British Columbia and holds a J.D./BBA LL.B., along with an advanced diploma in computer programming. He previously served as a Student Member of the Kwantlen Polytechnic University Board of Governors. He speaks English, Punjabi and Hindi.

name: Jessie Sunner
occupation: MLA; Minister of Mining and Critical Minerals; former lawyer
bio: Jessie Sunner is the incumbent MLA for Surrey-Newton and Minister of Mining and Critical Minerals, and previously served as Minister of Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills. Before entering politics she was a labour and human rights lawyer and trade unionist. She grew up in Surrey.

name: Mandeep Singh Dhaliwal
bio: Mandeep Singh Dhaliwal is the incumbent MLA for Surrey North. He owns Fixman Auto Glass Repair and Fixman Auto Glass Supplier in Surrey and holds a Bachelor of Arts from India. A member of the BC Sikh Motorcycle Club, he took part in fundraising rides for the BC Cancer Society and Khalsa Aid.

name: Parm Bhandol
bio: Parm Bhandol is a HandyDART operator who has lived in Surrey North for more than 10 years. He holds a BSc and an MSc in Mathematics.

name: Sahib Thind
bio: Sahib Thind is the founder and president of the Professor Mohan Singh Memorial Foundation, which organizes the annual Mela Gadri Babiyan Da at Bear Creek Park. He received B.C.'s Medal of Good Citizenship in 2017. He has lived in Surrey North for more than 40 years and is semi-retired from the construction industry.

name: Tanya Gupta
bio: Tanya Gupta is the OneBC candidate for Surrey North. She is a Notary Public who has owned and operated Tanya Gupta Notary Corporation since 2019 and also manages a gas station. She holds a Master of Applied Legal Studies from Simon Fraser University.

name: Yudhbir Gill
bio: Yudhbir Singh Gill is a sprinkler fitter apprentice who previously worked as a long-haul and dump truck driver. He came to Canada in 2012 and is the father of twin boys.

name: Bryan Tepper
bio: Bryan Tepper is the incumbent MLA for Surrey-Panorama and a former RCMP officer who served his last 10 years in Surrey. He was treasurer of the Mounted Police Professional Association of Canada during its court case over RCMP members' right to associate. He lives in Ocean Park with his wife Rona and has volunteered with several local organizations.

name: Jinny Sims
occupation: Former MLA and MP; former teachers' union president
bio: Jinny Sims was first elected as MLA for Surrey-Panorama in 2017 and served as B.C.'s Minister of Citizens' Services. She was previously the Member of Parliament for Newton-North Delta from 2011 to 2015. She is a past president of the BC Teachers' Federation and has worked as a radio talk show host.

name: Manav Manro
bio: Manav Manro is a local businessman with a background in hospitality who lives in Surrey-Panorama.

name: Nolen Scott
bio: Nolen Scott is an Assistant Director with nearly a decade of experience in British Columbia's film and television industry. He served two terms on the Production Assistants Caucus Advisory Committee of the Directors Guild of Canada and is a co-founder and board member of the Vancouver Venue Co-op.

name: Errol Povah
bio: Errol Povah served in the Royal Canadian Navy from 1974 to 1977 and worked 30 years with BC Ferries, retiring in 2008 as a Second (Navigating) Officer. He has volunteered with causes including anti-tobacco initiatives, Greenpeace and the Sea Shepherd Conservation Society.

name: Jessy Sahota
bio: Jessy Sahota is a police officer who was named one of the International Association of Chiefs of Police's Top 40 Under 40 in 2022. Since 2009 he has coached youth wrestlers with the Yo-Bro Yo-Girl Youth Initiative, and he won a national wrestling championship while at Simon Fraser University. He received the Queen's Platinum Jubilee Award in 2022.

name: Judy Higginbotham
occupation: Former Surrey city councillor; former teacher
bio: Judy Higginbotham served on Surrey City Council for 25 consecutive years after first being elected in 1983. A UBC graduate, she taught Physical Education and English for 12 years and later worked as a writer, editor and reporter. She served on the Metro Vancouver Board and for eight years on the Board of Directors of the Federation of Canadian Municipalities, and helped establish Tourism Surrey and the Surrey Foundation.

name: Sikander Kang
bio: Sikander Kang is a physiotherapist who established and manages five physiotherapy clinics in the Lower Mainland. He holds bachelor's and master's degrees in Physiotherapy. He is married with two children.

name: Todd Holowchak
bio: Todd Holowchak is the OneBC candidate for Surrey-Serpentine River. He co-founded a software company, was a vice president at a recruiting firm, and now leads business development for a B.C. software company. He previously served as president of the local BC Conservative riding association.

name: Bill McConnell
bio: Bill McConnell is a retired Red Seal electrician who taught electrical apprentices at BCIT for 19 years. He holds a diploma in Electrical Technology from BCIT and a Provincial Instructor's Diploma from Vancouver Community College, and worked on and supervised construction and industrial projects, including a high-voltage substation in North Vancouver.

name: Elenore Sturko
bio: Elenore Sturko is the Leader of CentreBC and has been an MLA since 2022, representing Surrey South and, since 2024, Surrey-Cloverdale. She served as a reservist in the Royal Canadian Air Force and then as an RCMP officer for 13 years, including as a frontline officer, a member of the Musical Ride and a media relations spokesperson.

name: Megan Knight
occupation: Mayor of White Rock; notary public
bio: Megan Knight is the Mayor of White Rock, elected in 2022, and previously served as a White Rock City Councillor from 2014 to 2018. Commissioned as a BC Notary Public in 1998, she ran a practice for 25 years. She has served on the Metro Vancouver Board and the TransLink Mayors' Council and has lived in the White Rock area for more than 46 years.

name: Parik Tahlan
bio: Parik Tahlan is a security professional who provides security for high-profile people and organizations. He holds a Master's degree in law specializing in Corporate and Commercial law and an MBA in marketing, and is a longtime supporter of the Canadian Cancer Society.

name: Amanda James
occupation: Vice President, Legal & Corporate Affairs, Eteros Technologies
bio: Amanda James is the OneBC candidate for Surrey-White Rock, where she has lived for nine years. She is Vice President, Legal & Corporate Affairs at Surrey-based manufacturer Eteros Technologies and previously held senior regional roles with the federal government. She holds a B.Sc. from UBC and an M.Sc. from the University of London.

name: Christine Kinnie
bio: Christine Kinnie is a secondary school secretary and longtime Surrey-White Rock resident. She earned a Diploma in General Studies from Kwantlen Polytechnic University and serves as a Lay Chaplain and Service Leader with the South Fraser Unitarians. In 2025 she was the Green Party of Canada candidate for South Surrey-White Rock.

name: Darryl Walker
occupation: Former Mayor of White Rock; former union president
bio: Darryl Walker is a former Mayor of White Rock and past President of the BC General Employees' Union. He has lived in White Rock for decades.

name: Trevor Halford
bio: Trevor Halford was first elected as MLA for Surrey-White Rock in 2020. He most recently served as Official Opposition critic (Shadow Minister) for Transportation and Infrastructure, ICBC and Affordability, BC Transit, and Sport, and previously for Mental Health and Addictions and TransLink. He was born and raised in the community and is a graduate of Elgin Park Secondary and Trinity Western University.

name: Waqas Rana
bio: Waqas Rana is a CPA, CMA with bachelor's and master's degrees in Accounting and Finance and a career in banking and insurance. He lives in Surrey-White Rock with his wife and family.

name: Aman Singh
bio: Aman Singh is a civil and human rights lawyer who served as MLA for Richmond-Queensborough from 2020 to 2024, the first turban-wearing Sikh elected to the BC Legislature. He has served as a director of the Professor Mohan Singh Memorial Foundation and the Association of Legal Aid Lawyers and as a Governor of Kwantlen Polytechnic University. He lives in South Vancouver with his two children.

name: Deep Sandhu
bio: Deep Singh Sandhu is a businessman and longshoreman with a background in forestry, real estate and asset management, and a Vancouver resident of over 35 years. He holds a Bachelor of Commerce from the University of Northern British Columbia and is a former Reservist in the Canadian Armed Forces. He volunteers at Guru Nanak's Free Kitchen and with the Khalsa Diwan Society.

name: Francoise Raunet
bio: Françoise Raunet is a Vancouver School Board teacher, currently on leave while serving as a Vice President of the Vancouver Elementary and Adult Educators Society. She holds a Bachelor of Education, a BA in Psychology and an MA in International Studies, and worked in educational publishing in Taipei for five years. She was the BC Green candidate in Vancouver-Point Grey in 2011 and 2013.

name: Christian Bosio
bio: Christian Bosio is a mechanical engineer who worked in the clean hydrogen sector before co-founding a company in 2008 that grew to over 300 employees. He has volunteered as a youth soccer coach and has lived near Commercial Drive for over 12 years.

name: Kimball Cariou
bio: Kimball Cariou is a former editor of People's Voice newspaper and has often been a Communist candidate in east Vancouver since the mid-1990s. Born in Saskatchewan, he joined the Communist Party as a University of Alberta student and served as the party's Saskatchewan leader for a decade before moving to Vancouver in 1993. Now retired, he volunteers at the Centre for Socialist Education and is a leader of the Vancouver Peace Council.

name: Kyra Philbert
bio: Kyra Philbert is a registered nurse with more than a decade of experience in healthcare, as well as an artist and scholar. In 2022 she completed a BA in Gender, Race, Sexuality and Social Justice and a Master of Science in Nursing at the University of British Columbia.

name: Niki Sharma
occupation: MLA; Deputy Premier and Attorney General
bio: Niki Sharma has served as MLA for Vancouver-Hastings since 2021. She has served as Deputy Premier and Attorney General.

name: Phil Webb
bio: Phil Webb was born and raised in British Columbia and lives in Vancouver. He states that he has no legal training and has not previously held public office.

name: Phyllis Tang
occupation: Community outreach and public relations professional; music teacher
bio: Phyllis Tang has worked in community outreach and public relations, including at UBC and as a Constituency Assistant to a Richmond-Queensborough MLA, and has taught piano and music theory for more than 25 years. She completed graduate studies in Ethnomusicology and ran for Vancouver City Council in 2018. She is Treasurer of the Marpole Neighbourhood House and lived in Vancouver-Hastings for more than 22 years.

name: Adam Hawk
bio: Adam Hawk holds a Commerce degree from Concordia University and has worked in the organic and natural foods sector. Originally from Montréal, he has lived in Vancouver since 2006 and has served on the boards of the Vancouver Greens and Velopalooza Bike Festival. He is a member of HUB Cycling and Vision Zero Vancouver.

name: Aron Lageri
occupation: Health care manager; medical imaging technologist
bio: Aron Lageri has more than 22 years of experience in health care, beginning as a medical imaging technologist at BC Children's Hospital and later serving as manager of the False Creek Surgical Centre. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Radiology and a postgraduate certificate in Long-Term Care Administration, and has served on the board of the Canadian Association of Medical Radiation Technologists.

name: Mable Elmore
bio: Mable Elmore is the incumbent MLA for Vancouver-Kensington, elected five times, and the first MLA of Filipino descent in BC. In 2025 she became Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, and in 2022 she was appointed Parliamentary Secretary for Anti-Racism Initiatives.

name: Alan Beesley
bio: Alan Beesley practised law in Vancouver for over a decade and later operated a fish buying station and the Ice House Oyster Bar in Tofino. He holds a B.A. and an LLB from UBC and was admitted to the BC Bar in 1989 and the New York Bar in 1991. He has volunteered as a Red Cross Site Team Lead and as an international election observer in Ukraine.

name: Jaime Stein
bio: Jaime Stein is Director for Western Canada at the Friends of Simon Wiesenthal Center and previously spent two decades in broadcasting and technology, including senior roles at Hootsuite. He holds an MBA from the Rotman School of Management and a Bachelor of Journalism from Toronto Metropolitan University. He was born and raised in Vancouver and has served as Vice Chair of CLEAR (Canadians for Leading Edge Alzheimer's Research).

name: John Atoyebi
bio: John Atoyebi is a lawyer and Principal Legal Counsel at Kebuiii Global Law Corporation who previously served as a Magistrate and District Court Judge in Nigeria and as an Investigator with the Office of the Ombudsperson of British Columbia. He is Executive Director of the BC Black Advocacy Society and serves on the City of Vancouver's Persons with Disabilities Advisory Committee. He received a BC Achievement Foundation Community Award in 2026.

name: Sunita Dhir
bio: Sunita Dhir was elected as MLA for Vancouver-Langara in 2024 and has served as Parliamentary Secretary for International Credentials. For nearly two decades she worked with SUCCESS supporting newcomers. She has lived in South Vancouver and Marpole for three decades.

name: Alex Muir
bio: Alexander Muir is a Vancouver-born University of British Columbia political science student who previously studied at University College Dublin. He has worked as a communications staffer in the Office of the Leader of the Official Opposition in Ottawa. He has represented Team BC in rugby and Canada's U20 national team.

name: Christine Boyle
occupation: MLA; community organizer and United Church minister
bio: Christine Boyle is a community organizer and ordained United Church minister who was elected MLA for Vancouver-Little Mountain in 2024 and served as Minister of Housing and Municipal Affairs. She previously served as a Vancouver City Councillor, where she led the development of Vancouver's Climate Emergency Action Plan.

name: Sarah MacLeod
bio: Sarah MacLeod spent more than a decade as an assistant director in the film industry on productions in Montreal, Toronto and Vancouver. She has since worked in fundraising and advocacy for healthcare, environmental and humanitarian causes, and has spoken at Vancouver City Council meetings and public hearings on issues including tree canopy, supportive housing and reconciliation.

name: Alex McMillan
occupation: Consultant; former interim CEO of BC Chamber of Commerce
bio: Alex McMillan served as interim CEO of the British Columbia Chamber of Commerce and runs a consultancy practice he started in 2020. He began his career as a senior political staffer and provincial civil servant, then worked at a national public relations firm and in government relations for a forestry company. He lives in Vancouver with his wife and two daughters.

name: Beatrice Sharpe
bio: Beatrice Sharpe is a University of Victoria student in Political Science and Environmental Studies and a former Chair of the Young BC Greens. She chairs Green Nation Collective Changemakers, previously worked as Canvass Director with the Ancient Forest Alliance, and published the poetry collection A Message from Our Mother.

name: David Eby
bio: David Eby is a lawyer who studied at the University of Waterloo and Dalhousie University and worked as a human rights lawyer in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside from 2005. First elected MLA for Vancouver-Point Grey in 2013, he served as Attorney General and Housing Minister before becoming BC's 37th Premier in 2022; he was re-elected in 2024. He is Premier of British Columbia.

name: Michael Davis
occupation: Retired communications and government relations firm principal
bio: Michael Davis recently retired as principal of a Vancouver communications and government relations firm and previously served as Director of Communications for Canada's Minister of Justice and Attorney General. He has served on non-profit boards since 1996, founded OurKidsClimate.ca, and holds a Master of Arts in Professional Communications from Royal Roads University. He lives in Kitsilano.

name: Callista Ryan
bio: Callista Ryan is a communications professional who has worked with the BC Public Service on communications and engagement, served as a communications and public affairs executive for a non-profit serving post-secondary students, and advises organizations on public policy, government relations and communications.

name: Carson Binda
occupation: Former BC Director, Canadian Taxpayers Federation
bio: Carson Binda was the B.C. Director of the Canadian Taxpayers Federation, which he joined in 2022, and previously worked in senior roles on municipal, provincial and federal political campaigns while studying at the University of British Columbia. He served as a logistics officer in the Canadian army reserves and lives in Vancouver.

name: Dallas Brodie
bio: Dallas Brodie is the MLA for Vancouver-Quilchena and interim leader of OneBC, which she co-founded in June 2025. She was elected as a BC Conservative in 2024 and was removed from that party's caucus in March 2025. Before politics she worked as a lawyer and broadcaster.

name: Douglas Courtemanche
bio: Dr. Douglas Courtemanche is a semi-retired craniofacial surgeon and health researcher with more than 35 years of practice in BC, and a Clinical Professor in UBC's Department of Surgery since 2008. He has served as Medical Staff President at BC Children's and Women's Hospital and President of the BC Medical Association's Section of Plastic Surgery. He grew up in Vancouver-Quilchena.

name: Petra Kuret
bio: Petra Kuret is a business executive who was Accenture's Managing Partner for British Columbia and later Senior Vice President of Strategy and Transformation at Vancity Credit Union, and has worked with an AI company since 2021. She chairs the board of Mosaic, holds an Honours BA in Political Science from Carleton University, and has lived in Vancouver-Quilchena for more than 40 years.

name: Adrian Dix
bio: Adrian Dix has been MLA for Vancouver-Renfrew since being elected in 2005. He served as Minister of Health from 2017 to 2024 and as Minister of Energy and Climate Solutions for nearly two years.

name: Lisa Prescott
bio: Lisa Prescott holds degrees in Industrial Engineering (BSc) and Mechanical Engineering (MSc) and worked in the public sector for more than 20 years, including senior roles with the City of Vancouver and BC Hydro. She now works as a consultant and has lived in Vancouver since 2003.

name: Rebecca Haber
bio: Rebecca Haber is a public health professional with more than 15 years of experience and science degrees from McGill University and the University of British Columbia. She has lived in East Vancouver for 17 years, serves on the board of an East Vancouver community garden, and helps run her family farm in Burnaby.

name: Tom Ikonomou
bio: Tom Ikonomou has worked as a licensed realtor since 2008, previously ran his own restaurants for 18 years, and has more than 23 years of security experience in the film industry. He is an Army veteran and former volunteer firefighter, serves as Treasurer of the Canadian Order of AHEPA Chapter CJ31 in Burnaby, and has lived in Vancouver since 2016.

name: Colin Smith
bio: Colin Smith is the owner/operator of a construction management firm in Kitsilano, with an academic background in law, international relations and sociology. He has served on community boards including the Kitsilano Area Childcare Society and has lived in the Vancouver-South Granville area for over 30 years.

name: Lara Honrado
occupation: Community relations and AI public-engagement professional
bio: Lara Honrado led community relations for Vancouver's former mayor and worked on the City of Vancouver's 2020-2029 cultural plan. She works with the United Nations and AI experts on public understanding of technology's impacts, serves on the board of 221A, and is a longtime Vancouver resident and parent of two.

name: Lisa Phillips
occupation: Finance and technology professional; business owner
bio: Lisa Phillips is a third-generation Vancouverite, finance and technology professional and business owner who holds a BSc in Mathematics from UBC. She has eight years of board governance experience, including with independent and alternative schools, and has volunteered helping people with housing, social programs and tax filing.

name: Maria J Cruz
bio: Maria J. Cruz works as an Outreach Worker in the Vancouver School Board's Adult Education program and has worked as a culture and heritage planner and collections care consultant. She holds a BA in Theatre and Art History from UBC and a Master of Museum Studies from the University of Toronto, has been a UBCP/ACTRA member for nearly 30 years, and has lived in South Granville for 15 years.

name: Salvatore Vetro
occupation: Former HandyDART driver; small business owner
bio: Salvatore Vetro is the OneBC candidate for Vancouver-South Granville. He drove a HandyDART van for 25 years and helped found the Kitsilano Showers Program for people experiencing homelessness. He helped lead the 2011 Fight HST campaign.

name: Amanda Burrows
bio: Amanda Burrows is Executive Director of First United in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside, where she led a $94-million redevelopment including Indigenous supportive housing. She previously ran for Mayor of Vancouver, holds a master's in museum studies from the University of Toronto, and is a renter in Chinatown.

name: Jordan Zheng McIntosh
bio: Jordan Zheng McIntosh was born in Vancouver, works as a mineral exploration field worker and is enrolled in a bachelor's degree program in geological engineering. On October 15, 2026, the BC Conservatives said he was no longer a Conservative candidate and would not sit in caucus if elected.

name: Robert Crooks
bio: Robert Crooks was elected leader of the Communist Party of BC in 2025. He began in politics as a tenant organizer in Winnipeg and later worked as a front-line worker and development coordinator for a youth-serving community organization in Winnipeg's Point Douglas neighbourhood. He is serving a third term as an executive member of the Canadian Network on Cuba.

name: Tanya Webking
occupation: Frontline housing and community support worker
bio: Tanya Webking is Dene and German, with roots in the Tłı̨chǫ Nation in the Northwest Territories. She has spent decades working on the frontlines of housing, healthcare and community support systems in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside.

name: Dion Weisner
occupation: Senior staffer, Office of the Leader of the Official Opposition
bio: Dion Weisner works in public policy and research and is a senior staffer in the Office of the Leader of the Official Opposition. He previously worked in sales and marketing for Harbour Air and on game operations for the University of Victoria basketball team and the Victoria HarbourCats.

name: Scott MacDonald
bio: Scott MacDonald is a retired physician who practised primary care in Vancouver from 2004 to 2026 with a focus on addictions medicine, and earlier served as Medical Director of Casey House Hospice in Toronto and as a military physician in Halifax. He holds a BSc in Biochemistry from Mount Allison University and a medical degree from Dalhousie University, and ran federally in Vancouver Centre for the Green Party of Canada in 2025.

name: Spencer Chandra Herbert
bio: Spencer Chandra Herbert has represented Vancouver-West End in the Legislature since 2008. He has served as Minister of Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation, Minister of Tourism, Arts, Culture and Sport, and Deputy Speaker, and founded Vancouver's Rent Bank. He was previously an artist and an elected Vancouver Park Board Commissioner.

name: Margareta Dovgal
bio: Margareta Dovgal is an economic commentator and policy analyst who has testified before parliamentary committees and worked in economic development advocacy. She co-founded the Indigenous Partnerships Success Showcase and has volunteered with the BC Schizophrenia Society and the Rotary Club of Vancouver Waterfront. She holds a BA from UBC and a Master of Public Administration from University College London.

name: Priyan Samarakoone
bio: Priyan Samarakoone is a housing and civil litigation lawyer who was called to the BC Bar in 2013, worked seven years with Access Pro Bono BC, and later founded his own law firm. He holds a BSc in Biology from UBC and an LLB from Nottingham Law School, chaired the Vancouver Green Party board from 2022 to 2024, and has lived in the riding for 16 years.

name: Sam Chandola
bio: Sam Chandola is a technology entrepreneur who arrived in Canada in 2012, founded several technology companies and sold three of them. In 2020 he founded First Fund, a pre-seed fund that has invested in BC startups. He holds a Bachelor's degree in Philology from Germany and has been based in Yaletown for more than a decade.

name: Terry Yung
bio: Terry Yung is a former Vancouver Police Department officer whose roles included Financial Crime Detective, and he was the longest-serving Board Chair of SUCCESS. Elected MLA for Vancouver-Yaletown in 2024, he served as Minister of State for Community Safety and Integrated Services.

name: Blair Visscher
bio: Blair Visscher has taught in School District 22 since 2022 and is pursuing doctoral research on wildfire evacuation communication at UBC Okanagan, where she holds bachelor's degrees in political science and education. She previously worked as a conflict resolution specialist in Fort McMurray, has served two terms as a UBC Okanagan Senator, and previously ran federally in Vernon–Lake Country–Monashee.

name: Chantel Gibbs
bio: Chantel Gibbs is the OneBC candidate for Vernon-Lumby, where she was born and raised. She holds a B.A. in Business Administration and a B.Sc. in Chemistry from Trinity Western University and has held the CPA, CGA designation since 2016. She serves as a volunteer director with the Canadian National Christian Foundation.

name: Harwinder Sandhu
bio: Harwinder Sandhu is the MLA for Vernon-Lumby, first elected in 2020, and a longtime Vernon resident. She worked as a healthcare worker for over two decades and is a mother of three.

name: Kevin Acton
occupation: Mayor of Lumby; registered massage therapist
bio: Kevin Acton is Mayor of Lumby, first elected to council in 2008 and mayor since 2009, and has represented Lumby on the Regional District of North Okanagan for 18 years, including as board chair. He is a registered massage therapist and partner at Bloom Wellness Centre, a former B.C. Ambulance Service paramedic, and has lived in the area since 1991.

name: Grace Lore
occupation: MLA; anti-violence advocate and academic instructor
bio: Grace Lore is an anti-violence advocate, academic instructor and researcher who has been elected twice as MLA. She has served as Parliamentary Secretary for Gender Equity, Minister of State for Childcare, and Minister of Children and Family Development.

name: Joachim Agou
bio: Joachim Agou was nominated as the BC Conservative candidate in Victoria-Beacon Hill. On October 8, 2026, interim leader Lorne Doerkson said he was no longer a Conservative candidate and would not serve in caucus if elected.

name: Rajinder S. Sahota
bio: Rajinder S. (Raj) Sahota is a Victoria-born litigator who holds Commerce and Law degrees from the University of Victoria and a Master of Laws from the London School of Economics. After working in corporate law in Toronto and New York, he has practised personal injury, human rights and class-action law in Victoria for nearly two decades, and has served more than a decade on the board of Pacifica Housing Advisory Association.

name: Carolyn Howe
occupation: Teacher; president of Greater Victoria Teachers' Association
bio: Carolyn Howe has taught at South Park Family School since 2005 and has been president of the Greater Victoria Teachers' Association since 2024. She holds degrees in music and education from the University of Victoria and is a choral conductor and performer.

name: Nina Krieger
bio: Nina Krieger first ran for public office in 2024 and has served as Minister of Public Safety and Solicitor General and as Parliamentary Secretary for Arts and Film. She previously served as Executive Director of a Holocaust museum in Western Canada.

name: Tim Taylor
occupation: Real estate professional and property manager
bio: Tim Taylor is a licensed real estate sales professional, property manager and strata manager in Victoria. He has chaired the Victoria Real Estate Board's Commercial Division, chaired the Kiwanis Housing Society for Seniors, served as president of the Victoria West Housing Society, and was a founding director of the CRD Housing Action Team.

name: Adam Frank
bio: Adam Frank is a Red Seal electrician who has worked on solar power projects and holds a bachelor's degree from Western University and a diploma in radio broadcasting. He led the Kelowna Climate Save movement from 2019 to 2022 and is a co-founder, board member and coach with the Kelowna Water Polo Club.

name: George Morgan
bio: George Morgan has lived in West Kelowna since age six, holds a bachelor's degree in physics from UBC Okanagan and is working toward a master's in mechanical engineering. He has volunteered at Kelowna General Hospital, worked six years as a swimming instructor and lifeguard, and serves as a director on the Central Okanagan Crime Stoppers board.

name: Macklin McCall
bio: Macklin McCall is the MLA for West Kelowna-Peachland and a former RCMP officer with 19 years of service, including in a Police and Crisis Team role. He grew up on a family farm in Okanagan Falls, studied criminology, psychology and sociology at OUC in Penticton, and has lived in West Kelowna for 15 years.

name: Arwa Shurab
bio: Arwa Shurab is a Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant, leadership coach and North Shore resident who holds a Master's degree in Global Leadership from Royal Roads University. She founded HERVOICE, a women's leadership initiative, and serves as a board director with the North Shore Restorative Justice Society.

name: Caroline Elliott
occupation: Public policy think tank senior fellow; policy consultant
bio: Caroline Elliott is a senior fellow with a public policy think tank and holds a PhD in Political Science from Simon Fraser University, where she taught B.C. politics. She previously advised the provincial ministers of Transportation and Environment under the Gordon Campbell government and runs a policy consulting business. She lives in North Vancouver.

name: Honieh Barzegari
occupation: Physician by training; healthcare and technology leader
bio: Honieh Barzegari is a physician by training who practised medicine in rural Iran before building a career in healthcare, technology and business in Canada. She served as a Ministerial Advisor with the Government of British Columbia, sits on the Langara College Board of Governors, and co-chairs KPU's Health and Science Committee.

name: Naomi Chocyk
bio: Naomi Chocyk is the OneBC candidate for West Vancouver-Capilano. She studied Political Science and International Relations at UBC and worked as a provincial political aide and constituency assistant. She was the People's Party of Canada candidate in Vancouver Granville in 2019 and the BC Libertarian candidate in Vancouver-False Creek in 2020.

name: Ayla Dumais
bio: Ayla Dumais was raised in Squamish and is a member of Prophet River First Nation. She works as a Policy and Stakeholder Relations Advisor in the Office of the Leader of the Official Opposition and previously worked in community relations with Woodfibre LNG.

name: Dan Wood
bio: Dan Wood is a housing and real estate professional who works at a provincial Crown organization negotiating leases and land agreements for housing sites. He holds a BA in Political Science and Economics and an MA in Asia Pacific Policy from UBC, has served as CentreBC's Communications Chair, and has lived in West Vancouver since 2023.

name: Jeremy Valeriote
bio: Jeremy Valeriote was elected MLA for West Vancouver–Sea to Sky in 2024, the first BC Green elected on the BC mainland. He has a background in environmental consulting, previously served as a Councillor for the Town of Gibsons, and holds an engineering degree and a Master's in leadership studies from Royal Roads University.

name: Michelle Livaja
bio: Michelle Livaja was born and raised in the Lower Mainland and has lived on Bowen Island for 26 years. She has served on her union's executive council, as a delegate to the local Labour Council, and as a board member for Metro Vancouver Alliance.
